## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference program's documentation):

```text
MP4 reader / writer of the video_processor testbench (PyAV:
  the FFmpeg libraries, `pip install av`). The SystemVerilog testbench reads
  and writes animated GIFs (video_tb_lib/gif_io.sv); this script turns a
  camera video (MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM: H.264, HEVC, ...) into the GIF the
  testbench sends through the camera, and the tracked GIF the testbench
  writes back into an MP4:
    to-gif   decode the video from a start time at a frame rate (frames
             picked at start + k / fps, nearest decoded frame), scale each
             to fit the tracking frame (320 x 240 by default, aspect kept,
             width a multiple of 4, height even; area filter) and write a looping GIF (a 256-colour palette of
             its own per frame, no dithering; delay 1 / fps)
    to-mp4   encode an animated GIF (the tracked output) as H.264 MP4
             (yuv420p, CRF 18), every pixel scaled up SCALE times (nearest:
             the 1-pixel boxes stay sharp), the GIF's frame delays kept
    info     size, frame rate, length and codec of a video
  scripts/run_sim.sh calls it for --gif=<video> (see there).
```

Per function:

```text
fit: w x h scaled to fit mw x mh, aspect kept (never up); width a multiple of 4, height even (the
camera's Bayer pattern and the 4-pixel feature cells).

read_video: Frames (PIL RGB) of the video at start + k / fps, k = 0 .. frames - 1 (0: to the end), scaled
to fit fit_w x fit_h.

gif_palette: A frame as the GIF holds it: a palette of its own (median cut, 256 colours, no dithering).

gif_colours: The RGB colours of a frame after the GIF round trip (what the testbench sends).

write_gif: Looping GIF, a palette of its own per frame (median cut, no dithering), delay 1 / fps.

gif_to_mp4: The GIF's frames as H.264 MP4, scaled up `scale` times (nearest), its frame delays kept.

write_mp4: PIL RGB frames, each shown delays[k] ms, as H.264 MP4 (yuv420p; odd sizes padded to even). An MP4
frame lasts until the next one starts, so the last frame is written once more at the end time: its
delay (a held last frame) is kept.
```

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the program.

```text
// Industry reference check - mp4_io.py (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] CompuServe, "Graphics Interchange Format Version 89a" (1990),
//   https://www.nayuki.io/page/gif89a-specification-html (LZW minimum code size, clear = 2^min,
//   EOI = clear + 1, code width grows when the next code reaches 2^width, 12-bit maximum,
//   255-byte sub-blocks, graphic control extension); LZW walkthrough
//   https://giflib.sourceforge.net/whatsinagif/lzw_image_data.html; NETSCAPE2.0 loop extension
//   (de facto)
//   [2] P. Heckbert, "Color image quantization for frame buffer display", SIGGRAPH 1982 pp.
//   297-307 (median cut: split the box with the largest range at the median of its longest
//   axis)
//   [3] ITU-T H.264 / ISO/IEC 14496-10 (4:2:0 needs even frame sizes) in an ISO/IEC 14496-14
//   MP4 container, written through PyAV / libx264
// Published algorithm / rules:
//   GIF frames with per-frame median-cut palettes; H.264 4:2:0 MP4 with even sizes.
// Comparison with this program (section 6):
//   Matches: PIL median-cut quantisation, frame delays kept, even padding for 4:2:0, last frame
//   held.
// Result: in line with the reference; no TODO.
```
